To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) video games provide a means of reasserting the racialized violence, gendered hierarchies, and territorial claims of empire, 2) video games work to resecure the racial, gendered, and national boundaries that were destabilized by 9/11 and its aftermath, and 3) video games are an important site of struggle for the meaning of race, nationhood, and gender in a post-9/11 context.
video games have aff orded the production of interactive spaces for the re-assertion of race and nation in the context of the ‘War on terror’.

(1) video games are a key site for the production of racialized violence, (2) video games are also a site for the production and reiteration of the colonial categories of race and culture, and (3) video games are an important site for the production, reproduction, and contestation of territoriality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which video games are used as a means of reasserting and redefining the nation-state in the wake of the September 11th attacks.
how video games are a part of the ‘War on terror’ and the ways that they reify the racialized and gendered violence that underlies the ‘War on terrorism’.
the ways in which video games are a site for the production of knowledge and meaning about race, nation, gender, and empire.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the video game industry has a long history of producing games that are not only racist, but are also sexist.
the video games industry has a significant role in the production of consent and the maintenance of the status quo in the post-9/11 world.
video games are a powerful medium of cultural production that can be used to reinforce the dominant ideology and to perpetuate the racialization of others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

video games are not only an important site for understanding the production of consent in a globalizing world, but are a crucial medium for the production of racialized violence and the reproduction of racialized terror.
the video games we analyze, while ostensibly about the war in Iraq, are actually about the war at home, a war that is waged against the very notion of a multicultural, multiracial America.
the video games under consideration are part of the ‘culture wars’ and are a form of popular culture that is a site of struggle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the racialized violence and displaced terror of the ‘War on terror’ have been reasserted through a reterritorializing of the nation and a rearticulation of racial difference in the video game.
video games are an important site of struggle over the meaning of the US empire.
the racialized violence in these games is a form of ‘displaced terror’, which is a way of managing the insecurities of the post-9/11 era by displacing them onto the bodies of racialized others.
